title: Reversal Red (SBL FBEOD)
author: Zayaan A.
desc:
this is a theoretically optimal sbl fbeod (full body every other day) plan with a focus on explosivity and improving athleticism. Also intended to be done in conjunction with zone 2 cardio on training days.  

this program is intended to be done as part of my limitless series, alongside my mobility/plyometrics plan (lapse blue), but is completely useable standalone.

the plan should (ideally) be repeated as follows, with a rest day inbetween each, alternating from A to B
- A:
  - AM: FBEOD (Lower Bias)
  - PM: Mobility -> Zone 2 Cardio
- B:
  - AM: FBEOD (Upper Bias)
  - PM: Plyo -> Zone 2 Cardio

Boostcamp Specific Notes:
- Translate RPE instead to RiR, ie RPE10 = 0RiR, RPE9 = 1RiR, ...
- 0 RiR is not failure, but wherein the next rep would fail

Hypertrophy:
- full body warmup done at start of session, 5 minutes on low intensity cardio of choice (stairmaster, incline walk... )
- Rest between sets until heart rate returns to baseline; but likely time between setting up exercises is enough
- exercise ordering is intentional, but can be swapped based on goal biases
- Test failure on a given joint action ideally at least once every 2 weeks, 
- consistently taking sets to failure will likely lead to the plan's volume being unsustainable
- avoid significantly lengthening muscles such that leverage is lost ... the benefit to hypertrophy is outweighed by the increase in muscle damage, and subsequent recovery demand
- for all cuffed/unilateral exercises (where applicable)
 - bluetooth handle
 - bend knees to lower CoG
 - rest 20-30s between sides


Cardio:
- Should be scheduled as far after hypertrophy training as possible, but on the same days as training - to prevent interference with recovery
- it is worth timing ~0.8g/kg/hr carbs ~1hr before

Programming Decisions: 
- RiR chosen so that volume is recoverable
- it is reasonable and probably optimal to swap a given exercise for one with an equivalent joint action if it is preferable to your situation (sequencing, setup, mobility, preference whatever)
  - exercise decisions were generally made as to maximise stability and progressive overloadability.
- Rep ranges chosen can be vaguely analogised to the minimum percentage increase when progressively overloaded, such that exercises where overloading is more difficult have higher rep ranges

Useful Resources:
- Discussion on volume, with authors of primary dose-response relationship meta analyses alongside jeff nippard
  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lbE-WU--Qp0
- Comprehensive reading on micronutrition, consequences, and sources
  https://lpi.oregonstate.edu/mic
- Plyometrics progression / decisions loosely influenced by work from dr john rusin

can be substituted for SLDL

Lean far back as possible to bias rec fem
can be substituted for lying

Unilateral preacher curl, or a recline curl
Ensure arm angle is below 45 degrees, stop when dumbbell touches shoulders, avoid excessive stretching
unilateral, cuffed, bt handle, brace opposite arm on pulley, keep elbow in single position
internally rotate humerus, align cable to be at 90deg when lateral head maximally extended, widen stance to lower CoG

Unilateral Cuffed, bt handle, neutral grip
stand very close to cable
standard d-handle, brace tricep against cable pillar and extend
if cannot do bodyweight, banded preferrable to machine assisted, ensure chin over bar
avoid too deep of a stretch on eccentric, stop ~5-10deg below parallel
close, neutral, false grip. machine is fine
avoid deep stretch on eccentric, pause before weight pulls you into stretch. stop concentric when elbow flexion occurs
lying on floor facing away from cable, foam roller under low back, stop when abs lose leverage and hip flexors take over
Switch to hanging if able to do so in a stable way, goal is for hip to move off of pad for spinal flexion
